findings.problem: The same four-line argument appears six times in the file. The base-component version appears at lines 38–40, 84–87 and 88–91. The tangent-component version appears at lines 41–44, 92–96 and 97–101. Each block does the same three things: unfold `polynomialFirstJetHom` with `change`, rewrite with `dualEvalLie_base` or `dualEvalLie_tangent`, and apply `eval_mem_iff_coefficients`. The only things that vary are the polynomial (A or C) and the hypotheses used. The long `have` blocks hide the real mathematical content of `polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers`: apply the dual lemma to the first jets of A and C.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two small lemmas in the `NilpotentLieBCHGroup` namespace before `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients`:

theorem dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem (U : LieSubalgebra ℚ L) (A : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) (hAU : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ U) (t h : σ → ℚ) : dualBaseLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ U := by
  change dualBaseLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ U
  rw [dualEvalLie_base]
  exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients U.toSubmodule _).mpr hAU t

theorem dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem (V : Submodule ℚ L) (A : PolynomialGroup σ hnil) (hAV : ∀ α, coefficients A.coord α ∈ V) (t h : σ → ℚ) : dualTangentLinear (polynomialFirstJetHom t h A).coord ∈ V := by
  change dualTangentLinear (dualEvalLie t h A.coord) ∈ V
  rw [dualEvalLie_tangent]
  exact (eval_mem_iff_coefficients V _).mpr (directionalDerivative_mem_coefficientSubmodule V h A.coord hAV) t

Then `polynomialLogDerivative_mem_of_coefficients` becomes `dualLogDerivative_mem_of_invariant U V hUV _ (dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem U A hAU t h) (dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem V A hAV t h)`. In `polynomial_removal_preserves_derivative_layers`, replace lines 84–101 by passing `(dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem U A hAU t h) (dualBaseLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem U C hCU t h) (dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem V A hAV t h) (dualTangentLinear_polynomialFirstJet_mem V C hCV t h)` directly to `F.derivative_removal_preserves_quotient_layers`. Keep the final `simpa only [polynomialFirstJet_base, polynomialLogDerivative] using he`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 lines of copy-pasted proof. The `change` plus `rw` unfolding is written once, so a future change to `dualEvalLie` or `polynomialFirstJetHom` needs one edit. Each helper has a name that says what it does, so the main theorem reads as "first jets of A and C satisfy the hypotheses of the dual removal lemma" instead of four near-identical blocks that must be compared by eye.
